>_typeSymbols.ArgumentNullException.GetMembers("ThrowIfNull"); [](http://example.com/codeflow?start=45&length=61)

Is there any possibility this can return null?

>_typeSymbols.ArgumentNullException.GetMembers("ThrowIfNull"); [](http://example.com/codeflow?start=45&length=61)

Is there any possibility this can return null?

>Parse [](http://example.com/codeflow?start=78&length=5)

do we care which overload we are interested in? or we use all of them?

When generic Parse was introduced first time in .NET Core 2.0/.NET Standard 2.1, two overloads where added at the same time : `Parse<TEnum>(String)` and `Parse<TEnum>(String, Boolean)`. So it seems safe to assume that when there is a generic Parse, the overload `Parse<TEnum>(String)` exists

>IsNetCore [](http://example.com/codeflow?start=77&length=9)

ditto
same reason here, uses ImmutableArray which is not supported on net462
